version: Agent Builder: scheduled shutdown 2026-11-30; ChatKit (chatkit-python/js Apache-2.0); openai-guardrails-python (MIT)

facts.claim: Approval is required before any data is sent to a connector or remote MCP server by default; require_approval accepts 'always', 'never' or a never.tool_names object.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Safety guide: 'always enable tool approvals so end users can review and confirm every operation'; in Agent Builder use the human approval node.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Guardrails provide input checks (PII redaction, jailbreak detection) described as 'not foolproof'.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: MCP/connector tool calls require approval by default (require_approval='always' semantics); Agent Builder offers a human-approval node; Guardrails are optional and documented as not foolproof.

facts.claim: Agent Builder workflows can be deployed via ChatKit using a workflow ID or as downloaded Agents SDK code that the customer runs.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D02.rationale: N/A for the hosted visual builder; code execution is via Responses API tools or the customer-run Agents SDK export.

D03.rationale: Not documented in the pages read.

facts.claim: OpenAI does not verify remote MCP servers; servers can change tool behaviour unexpectedly; prompt injection via server outputs is a documented risk.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: connector_id is deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026; use server_url or tunnel_id.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D05.rationale: Remote MCP servers need per-call approval by default and docs warn OpenAI does not verify them; Connector Registry governance details not verified; connector_id deprecated for models released after 2026-09-01.

facts.claim: Connectors require an OAuth access token supplied in the authorization field.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Guardrails docs: developers must implement safeguards against storing sensitive content; OpenAI disclaims liability for developer logging/retention.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D07.rationale: Connectors take an OAuth access token passed in each request (customer holds tokens); no vault-style secret isolation documented; Guardrails docs tell developers to avoid persisting blocked content.

D09.rationale: Not documented for Agent Builder in pages read.

facts.claim: Agent Builder: Preview shows per-node execution; Evaluate runs trace graders against selected traces.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: With store=true, API data is logged for 30 days unless Zero Data Retention is enabled.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D11.rationale: Preview runs show per-node execution; Evaluate runs trace graders on traces; API data with store=true is logged for 30 days.

facts.claim: With store=true, API data is logged for 30 days unless ZDR enabled; MCP servers' own retention policies apply.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D12.rationale: 30-day application-state retention with ZDR option; MCP third-party servers apply their own retention.

D13.rationale: SDK/UI toolkits are open source (ChatKit Apache-2.0, openai-guardrails-python MIT); packaging provenance not verified.

D14.rationale: Not verified; org-level connector governance in the Connector Registry was not documented in pages that could be fetched (openai.com announcement returned 403).

facts.claim: OpenAI asks that malicious MCP servers be reported to security@openai.com.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Third-party reports: HiddenLayer (Oct 2025) and Zenity Labs (Nov 2025) reported AgentKit Guardrails can be bypassed via prompt injection; no CVE/OpenAI advisory found.
facts.label: third-party-report

D15.rationale: No GitHub security advisories found for openai-guardrails-python, chatkit-python, chatkit-js, openai-agents-python/js (empty lists); MCP-server abuse reports go to security@openai.com; third-party research (HiddenLayer, Zenity) reported Guardrails bypasses without CVEs.
